video:video.video:title: पाँच सौ की प्लेट... खाना सिर्फ़ सौ पचास!
video:video.video:description: A ₹500 wedding plate contains only ~₹150 of real food — dal, rice, sabzi, ghee; the rest goes to labor, gas, utensils, transport, and the caterer's profit.\nपाँच सौ की शादी की प्लेट में असली खाना यानि दाल, चावल, सबज़ी, घी — लगभग सौ पचास रुपये का ही होता है; बाक़ी पैसा मज़दूरी, गैस-बरतन, ढुलाई और कैटरर के मुनाफे में जाता है।

video:video.video:title: 200 रुपये की बाल कटाई में नाई को 50 रुपये ही बचते है?
video:video.video:description: A ₹200 haircut puts only ~₹50 in the barber's pocket — with a ~₹12,000/month wage spread over ~260 cuts, each cut yields ~₹48, and the rest goes to rent, electricity, and shop costs.\nदो सौ रुपये की बाल कटाई में सिर्फ़ पचास रुपये नाई की जेब में बचते हैं — बारह हज़ार रुपये महीने की तनख़वाह लगभग 260 कटाई में हर कटाई पर लगभग अड़तालीस रुपये बचते हैं, और बाकी किराया‑बिजली‑दुकान के खर्च में जाते हैं।

video:video.video:title: 5 रुपये का अखबार... और लागत 15 रुपये? कैसे?
video:video.video:description: A ₹5 newspaper costs ₹15 to produce — paper, ink, printing, distribution and retailer margins all add up.\n₹5 का अखबार बनाने में ₹15 लगते हैं — कागज़, स्याही, छपाई, वितरण और दुकानदार का मार्जिन सब जोड़ता है।

video:video.video:description: ₹100 withdrawal costs ₹23 — it's not an ATM fee, it's the cost of keeping money sitting idle in machines. Roughly ₹21 lakh crore sits idle across India's ATMs.

video:video.video:title: बीस की बोतल... पांच की लागत!
video:video.video:description: A ₹20 1-litre bottled water costs less than 50 paise in real water — plastic alone is ~₹3; the plant sells for ₹10–14 and the retailer ₹20.

video:video.video:title: बीस की गोलगप्पे... पांच की लागत!
video:video.video:description: ₹20 plate of golgappes costs ₹5-6 to make, but restaurants sell them for ₹500. Street vendor earnings: small town ₹600, big city ₹1,100, metro hub ₹3,000/day.

video:video.video:title: बिजली बिल 0 — सोलर पैनल लगाने का हिसाब
video:video.video:description: How your electricity bill becomes zero with PM Surya Ghar Yojana — ₹78,000 subsidy for a 3kW system + ₹17,000 Rajasthan bonus. The math behind free electricity.

video:video.video:title: सौ के ride में ड्राइवर की जेब में कितना बचता है?
video:video.video:description: How much does a cab driver actually keep from a ₹100 ride? With the platform's commission now a daily subscription of ~₹67, drivers take home only about ₹40-50 per ride.

video:video.video:title: ₹5000 का टिकट — एयरलाइन को कितना मिलता है?
video:video.video:description: How much does an airline actually keep from a ₹5000 flight ticket? Base fare is roughly ₹3,600, but taxes, fuel, and airport charges make up the rest — only about ₹1,200 goes to the airline itself.

video:video.video:title: ₹10 Chai — Chaiwala Earnings?
video:video.video:description: How much does a chaiwala actually keep from a ₹10 cup of chai? Milk costs roughly ₹2, sugar ₹1, tea leaves ₹1, and gas plus the cup about ₹0.50 — a total cost of ~₹4.50, leaving ~₹5.50 per cup. But the real money is not in one cup — it is in the ~500 cups sold every day.

video:video.video:title: ₹300 Ticket — Cinema Owner Earnings?
video:video.video:description: How much does a cinema owner actually keep from a ₹300 ticket? Cinema halls share roughly 50% of net ticket revenue with the film distributor. But the real business is F&B — popcorn and cold drinks with ~75% margin.

video:video.video:title: ⛽ Petrol Pump Earning?
video:video.video:description: How much does a Petrol Pump Owner actually earn on ₹100? With margins of roughly ₹1-2 per litre, petrol pumps survive on volume — a single pump serves hundreds of vehicles daily. But the real profits come from the shop: lubricants, snacks, chai, and the convenience premium.
